sub_tasks.requirements: The AWQ per-channel scaling method, including scale search via s = sX^alpha grid search over alpha in [0,1] and weight clipping, is implemented per Section 3.2.
Weight-only group quantization primitive is implemented as the foundation used throughout AWQ.

Code has been implemented for a weight-only quantization function Q(W) that supports INT3 and INT4 bit-widths with a configurable per-group size (default 128) computing scale Delta from the absolute maximum within each group as in Equation 1.

verification.spec: Import the implemented quantization function Q(W) and confirm it accepts (weight_tensor, n_bit in {3,4}, group_size int, default 128). For each group, verify Delta is computed as max(|W_group|)/(2^(N-1)-1) and that the returned dequantized weights fall on Delta * integer grid within [-2^(N-1), 2^(N-1)-1]. Test with n_bit=3 and n_bit=4, group_size=128.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented so that the quantizer uses Delta = max(|W|) / (2^(N-1)) style scaling (symmetric or the asymmetric variant matching the released AWQ code) and rounds via round-to-nearest with integer clipping to the representable range.

verification.spec: On synthetic tensors, verify the quantizer computes Delta = max(|W_group|) / (2^(N-1) - 1) or the asymmetric variant used in the released AWQ code, applies round-to-nearest, and clips integer codes to the representable range; test that values outside the range are clipped and integer codes fall within [-(2^(N-1)-1), 2^(N-1)-1] for N=3,4.

sub_tasks.requirements: Round-trip quantize-dequantize of a random FP16 weight tensor at INT4-g128 recovers values with maximum absolute error bounded by half the per-group step size Delta, verifying the primitive behaves as an integer round-to-nearest quantizer.

verification.spec: Generate a random FP16 weight tensor of shape (out=256, in=512). Apply Q at INT4-g128, dequantize, and assert that max |W - Q(W)| <= Delta/2 for each group (where Delta = group_max_abs / 7). This verifies round-to-nearest behavior with correct per-group step size.

sub_tasks.requirements: Per-channel scaling transformation (scale weights by s, inverse-scale activations by 1/s) is implemented as an equivalent transformation applied before quantization.

Code has been implemented that, given a per-input-channel scale vector s, computes Q(W * s) and stores the reciprocal scaling s^-1 to be fused into the preceding operator (LayerNorm or previous linear) so that y = Q(W*s) * (X / s) mathematically equals the un-scaled linear up to quantization error.

verification.spec: Instantiate a small Linear layer with a preceding LayerNorm. Apply the scaling transform with a random per-input-channel s>0: multiply linear.weight by s along input dim and fuse 1/s into layernorm.weight/bias (or the previous linear). Verify forward outputs at FP16 match the un-scaled forward within 1e-3 relative tolerance, and that the stored scale exposes both s (on weight) and s^-1 (fused into predecessor).

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented to fuse the inverse scale s^-1 into the previous LayerNorm/RMSNorm weight (and bias, if present) and into the previous linear layer's output projection weight for attention Q/K/V and FFN up/gate projections, following the same fusion pattern as SmoothQuant.

verification.spec: Construct a small model with LayerNorm -> Linear (Q/K/V pattern); apply the fusion function with a per-channel scale s; verify (a) LayerNorm weight (and bias) are divided by s, (b) Linear weight input channels are multiplied by s, (c) output of the model on a random input before and after fusion differs by < 1e-4 in max-abs (numerically equivalent).

sub_tasks.requirements: With s = 1 (identity), the scaling transformation produces outputs numerically identical (up to FP16 precision) to the un-scaled quantized layer, confirming the transformation is a pure no-op at s=1.

verification.spec: Instantiate a quantized linear layer with the scaling transform applied at s = ones(in_features). Compare the forward output on random FP16 inputs to the equivalent quantized linear with no scaling applied. Assert bitwise-equal (or within 1e-6 relative) outputs.

sub_tasks.requirements: With arbitrary s > 0 applied to weights and 1/s inversely fused into activations/previous op, the FP16 (un-quantized) forward output is mathematically equivalent (within numerical tolerance) to the original, verifying scaling is a valid equivalent transformation.

verification.spec: For an FP16 (un-quantized) linear preceded by a LayerNorm, apply the equivalent transform with a random positive scale s (multiply W by s along in-dim, divide LN weight/bias by s). Verify forward output on random inputs matches the original within 1e-3 relative tolerance, confirming mathematical equivalence in the un-quantized limit.

Code has been implemented and run such that AWQ produces per-channel scales s = sX^alpha with a grid search of size 20 over alpha in [0,1] selecting the best alpha per linear layer

verification.spec: Import the AWQ scale-search routine; call it on a synthetic linear layer with cached activations; verify it evaluates exactly 20 alpha values on a uniform grid in [0,1] and returns the alpha minimizing MSE(Q(W*s)*X/s , W*X)
verification.paper_cite: Section 5.1 ("grid size of 20 to search for optimal α"); Equation 5

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented and run such that the quantization function Q(w) = Delta * Round(w / Delta) with Delta = max(|w|) / (2^(N-1)) is implemented and matches the paper's formulation (Equation 1).

verification.spec: Import the quantize function; for a random weight tensor w and N=3, compute Delta = max(|w|) / (2^(N-1)) = max(|w|)/4, then assert Q(w) == Delta * Round(w/Delta) elementwise and that Q(w) values lie on a Delta-spaced grid.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented and run such that the scaled quantization identity Q(w*s)*(x/s) is implemented, taking a per-channel scale s and applying it to weights before quantization and inversely to activations.

verification.spec: For weights w and activations x with per-channel scale s>1, implement scaled_forward(w, x, s) = Q(w*s) @ (x/s); assert that for s=1 the result equals Q(w) @ x, and for s!=1 the numerical output is close to Q(w) @ x within expected quantization error.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented and run such that the quantization error formula Err(Q(w*s)(x/s)) = Delta' * RoundErr * (1/s) is verified: the ratio of scaled error to unscaled error equals (Delta'/Delta) * (1/s).

verification.spec: For a random weight vector w and scale s>1 that does not change the group absmax (so Delta' ~ Delta), empirically compute mean |Q(w*s)/s - w| and mean |Q(w) - w|; assert the ratio is approximately (Delta'/Delta)*(1/s) within 10% tolerance.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented and run such that the AWQ scale-search objective L(s) = || Q(W * diag(s)) * (diag(s)^-1 * X) - W*X ||  is implemented and minimized over per-input-channel scales s.

verification.spec: Import the AWQ scale-search routine; for a small linear layer with random W and calibration X, run the search and confirm that (a) the returned scale s has same length as input channel dimension, (b) L(s_opt) <= L(s=1), (c) the fused (s^-1)*X can be absorbed into the previous layer's weights without changing outputs.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented and run such that the AWQ search space s = s_X^alpha is implemented, where s_X is the per-channel average magnitude of activations and alpha in [0,1] is a scalar swept via grid search of size 20.

verification.spec: Import AWQ scale search; verify that (a) s_X is computed as mean absolute activation per input channel from calibration data, (b) candidate scales are s = s_X**alpha for alpha values on a length-20 grid over [0,1], (c) alpha=0 corresponds to s=1 (no scaling), (d) the chosen alpha minimizes the reconstruction MSE.

verification.spec: Given a random INT4 weight tensor, pack using the {0,2,4,6,1,3,5,7} interleaving into uint32 words and then unpack; assert bit-exact recovery of the original INT4 values; also assert the packed byte layout matches the specified permutation

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented such that TinyChat's fused attention kernel performs QKV projection, on-the-fly RoPE, and KV-cache update in a single kernel launch.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented such that TinyChat's fused LayerNorm/RMSNorm kernel executes multiplication, division, and sqrt in a single kernel launch.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code implements SIMD-aware 4-bit weight packing where each 128-bit register holds 32 4-bit weights in the interleaved order w0, w16, w1, w17, ..., w15, w31.

verification.spec: Call TinyChat's weight-packing utility on a synthetic length-32 sequence of 4-bit weights [0..31]. Read back the packed bytes and assert the low nibbles of bytes 0..15 correspond to weights [0,1,2,...,15] and the high nibbles correspond to weights [16,17,...,31] (i.e., register layout w0,w16,w1,w17,...,w15,w31). Fail if any position differs.

sub_tasks.requirements: The NEON unpacking routine uses exactly 3 SIMD instructions per 32 packed weights (one AND with 0x0F mask for low nibbles, one shift-right by 4, and one AND for high nibbles).

verification.spec: Locate the NEON unpack routine in the TinyChat CPU backend. Assert it contains exactly one `vandq_u8` with a 0x0F mask constant, one `vshrq_n_u8` (or equivalent >>4 shift), and one additional `vandq_u8` (for the shifted high nibbles) per 128-bit register worth of weights. Verify no additional per-weight scalar unpacking is emitted.

sub_tasks.requirements: TinyChat dispatches quantized linear layers to the fused W4A16 kernel that performs on-the-fly dequantization (i.e., dequantized weights are never materialized to DRAM).

verification.spec: Monkey-patch or hook TinyChat's quantized-linear forward. Run a forward pass on a loaded AWQ model and assert (a) the hook is invoked with int4-packed weights (dtype indicates packed int, not fp16), (b) intermediate storage of a full FP16 dequantized weight matrix does not appear in allocator traces (peak allocation for that layer < 1.5x activation size), and (c) the output matches a reference `dequant-then-matmul` implementation within 1e-2.

sub_tasks.requirements: TinyChat pre-allocates the KV cache and performs cache updates inside the fused attention kernel (not via separate PyTorch ops).

verification.spec: Inspect TinyChat's generation loop: assert the KV-cache tensors are allocated once at model init (before the first forward) with shape [layers, batch, max_seq, num_heads, head_dim]. Then run a decode of 8 tokens and assert (a) no new KV-cache allocations occur after the first token (allocator peak stable), and (b) the attention kernel's launch signature includes the KV-cache pointers as in/out arguments (grep the kernel entrypoint).
